extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (algebraic geometers / computational algebraists) seeking reference for library procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (paraplanecurves.lib and resbinomial.lib) describing usage, assumptions, returns, and example behaviour for functions used in parametrization testing and E-resolution of binomial ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: testParametrization
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: testParametrization(f, rTT); f poly, rTT ring
Assume: The assumptions on the basering and the polynomial f are as required by Section D.5.4.3 [paraPlaneCurve], page 1112. The ring rTT has two variables and contains an ideal PARA (such as the ring obtained by applying Section D.5.4.3 [paraPlaneCurve], page 1112 to f).
Return: int which is 1 if PARA defines a parametrization of the curve {f=0} and 0, otherwise.
Theory: We compute the polynomial defining the image of PARA and compare it with f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shown: create ring and poly f, call paraPlaneCurve(f) to obtain a ring with ideal PARA, then setring RP1; PARA; testParametrization(f, RP1); returns 1 when PARA is a parametrization. Keep basering and polynomial assumptions as in paraPlaneCurve documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: testPointConic
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: testPointConic(p, r); p poly, r ring
Assume: assumes that p is a homogeneous quadratic polynomial in the first three ring variables of the current basering; Assumes that there is a (1x3) matrix named 'point' in r with entries from the ground field of r.
Return: returns 1 iﬀ the point named 'point', residing in r, lies on the conic given by p; 0 otherwise
Note: This method temporarily changes the basering to r. Afterwards, the basering will be the same as before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: compute a rational point ring S = rationalPointConic(p); then testPointConic(p, S) returns 1 and prints the conic and point information. Use when you have a conic polynomial p and a ring containing a 'point' matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: BINresol
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: BINresol(J); J ideal
Return: E-resolution of singularities of a binomial ideal J in terms of the affine charts, see example
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates loading LIB "resbinomial.lib", creating a ring and ideal J and calling list B=BINresol(J); then B[1] returns list of final charts and B[2] list of all charts. Output includes chart information (coefficients, number of vars, orderings, variable names).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eresol
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: Eresol(J); J ideal
Return: The E-resolution of singularities of J in terms of the affine charts, see example
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: calling Eresol(J) prints a prompt to press return after break points to step through output list. The returned list L contains information per chart; the manual shows inspecting L[1][1] for first chart information. Use for stepwise interactive inspection of E-resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: determinecenter
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: determinecenter(Coef,expJ,c,n,Y,a,listmb,flag,control3,Hhist); Coef, expJ, listmb, flag lists, c number, n, Y, control3 integers, a, Hhist intvec
Compute: next center of blowing up and related information, see example
Return: several lists defining the center and related information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates assembling data(J,...) then calling determinecenter(...) to compute the first center; returned lists include LL[1] index of variables in the center, LL[2] exponents of ideals J_4..J_1, LL[3] orders of those ideals, LL[4] critical values, LL[5] components of resolution function t, LL[6..8] lists of divisors and exceptional divisors, LL[9] auxiliary invariant and LL[10] intvec pointing last step where t dropped. Inspect these lists to get center and related invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blowupcenter
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: Blowupcenter(center,id,nchart,infochart,c,n,cstep);
center, infochart lists, id, nchart, n, cstep integers, c number
Compute: The blowing up at the chart IDCHART along the given center
Return: new affine charts and related information, see example
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: after computing center with determinecenter, prepare infochart and call Blowupcenter(...) to obtain L3; L3[1] is the current chart with fields (parent,Y,center,expJ,Coef,flag,Hhist,blwhist,path,hipercoef,hiperexp) and enumerated sons. Inspect L3 and its components to see new charts, their variable indices, exponents, exceptional divisors, and other bookkeeping. Many example outputs illustrate the structure and positions of sons and chart metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonhyp
rubrics_metrics.description:
Compute: The 'ideal' generated by the non hyperbolic generators of J
Return: lists with the following information newcoef,newJ: coeﬃcients and exponents of the non hyperbolic generators total-hyp,totalgen: coeﬃcients and exponents of the hyperbolic generators flaglist: new list saying status of variables
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the basering r is supposed to be a polynomial ring K[x,y], in fact, we work in a localization of K[x,y], of type K[x,y] y with y invertible variables. Example shows usage sequence: data(J,...) then maxEord(...); then New=Nonhyp(...,L2[2]); New[1] and New[2] give coefficient/exponent lists; New[3..] and other outputs list hyperbolic coefficients/exponents and updated flaglists. Use to separate hyperbolic and non-hyperbolic parts and update invertible-variable flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: identifyvar
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ring r = 0,(x(1),y(2),x(3),y(4),x(5..7),y(8)),dp; identifyvar(); returns a list [0,1,0,1,0,0,0,1]. Use at start to mark which variables are treated as invertible ('y' variables) vs standard variables ('x').

rubrics_metrics.name: Edatalist
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: Edatalist(Coef,Exp,k,n,flaglist);
Coef,Exp,flaglist lists, k,n, integers
Exp is a list of lists of exponents, k=size(Exp)
Compute: computes a list with the E-order of each term
Return: a list with the E-order of each term
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: prepare data(L=data(J,3,8)) then list EL=Edatalist(L[1],L[2],3,8,flag); EL contains E-order per term. Note: examples show behaviour in characteristic 0 and warn that computations in characteristic 2 should be done in char 0 (i.e., 'IN CHAR 2, COMPUTATIONS NEED TO BE DONE IN CHAR 0').

rubrics_metrics.name: EOrdlist
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: EOrdlist(Coef,Exp,k,n,flaglist);
Coef,Exp,flaglist lists, k,n, integers
Exp is a list of lists of exponents, k=size(Exp)
Compute: computes de E-order of an ideal given by a list (Coef,Exp) and extra information
Return: maximal E-order, and its position=number of generator and term
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: after data(J,4,8) call EOrdlist(...); Eo[1] is E-order, Eo[2] generator index giving E-order, Eo[3] term index giving E-order. Use when you need the maximal E-order and where it occurs in the generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxEord
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: maxEord(Coef,Exp,k,n,flaglist);
Coef,Exp,flaglist lists, k,n, integers
Exp is a list of lists of exponents, k=size(Exp)
Return: computes de maximal E-order of an ideal given by Coef,Exp
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: list M=maxEord(L[1],L[2],4,8,flag); M[1] gives the maximal E-order. Use prior to selecting centers or separating components based on E-order.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECoef
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: ECoef(Coef,expP,sP,V,auxc,n,flaglist);
Coef, expP, flaglist lists, sP, V, n integers, auxc number
Compute: The ideal E-Coeﬀ V(P), where V is a permissible hypersurface which belongs to the center
Return: list of exponents, list of coeﬃcients and classiﬁcation of the ideal E-Coeﬀ V(P)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show calling data(P,...) then list L2=ECoef(...); L2[1] are exponents of the E-Coefficient ideal with respect to x(1), L2[2] its coefficients and L2[3] a classification (type). Notes in examples warn: 'THE COMPUTATIONS ARE NOT CORRECT IN CHARACTERISTIC p>0' and 'E-order zero!' when characteristic-dependent; thus prefer char 0 for these computations. Use to compute E-coefficient ideal relative to a chosen hypersurface.

rubrics_metrics.name: elimrep
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: elimrep(L); L is a list
Compute: Eliminate repeated terms from a list
Return: the same list without repeated terms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: L=4,5,2,5,7,8,6,3,2; elimrep(L); returns [4,5,2,7,8,6,3]. Use to canonicalize lists by removing duplicates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emaxcont
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: Emaxcont(Coef,Exp,k,n,flag);
Coef,Exp,flag lists, k,n, integers
Exp is a list of lists of exponents, k=size(Exp)
Compute: Identify ALL the variables of E-maximal contact
Return: a list with the indexes of the variables of E-maximal contact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: after data(J,4,8) call list hyp=Emaxcont(L[1],L[2],4,8,flag); hyp[1] gives max E-order, hyp[2] returns list of hypersurfaces of E-maximal contact or 'empty list' if none. Use to determine permissible hypersurfaces for E-maximal contact; behaves differently depending on computed E-order (often zero) as shown in examples.
